title: Microsoft Entra Agent ID reaches general availability with agent blueprints, lifecycle governance and Conditional Access templates
summary: Microsoft's "What's new in Microsoft Entra Agent ID" page states that Agent ID is now generally available, bringing identity and access management to AI agents through purpose-built identity constructs, specialized OAuth flows, an Auth SDK sidecar for token acquisition, automated cascade deletion of agent identities, a preview wizard for creating agent identity blueprints, and sidecar or federation integration patterns for non-Microsoft agents on AWS, GCP and n8n. Governance adds access packages for both on-behalf-of and autonomous agents and sponsor lifecycle workflow templates that transfer sponsorship when a sponsor changes roles or leaves, to prevent orphaned agents, while new Conditional Access templates block sign-ins from high-risk agent identities and set separate policies for autonomous agents and for agents acting on behalf of users.
verification_note: URL fetched 2026-10-17; the Microsoft Learn page carries ms.date 2026-05-01 (last updated 2026-08-13) and opens by stating that Microsoft Entra Agent ID is now generally available. Confirmed from the page text: Auth SDK sidecar for token acquisition, cascade deletion and soft delete of agent identities, integration patterns for non-Microsoft agents on AWS, GCP and n8n, access packages for on-behalf-of and autonomous agents, sponsor lifecycle workflow templates to prevent orphaned agents, and Conditional Access templates for high-risk, autonomous and on-behalf-of agents. The blueprint and agent identity creation wizard is marked Preview on the page, so the summary says so.
